title: Comparing, Ordering & Rounding
description: Class 4 Maths: compare and order large numbers up to lakhs, and round numbers to the nearest 10, 100 and 1000 — with worked examples and free tests.

topics.title: Comparing & Ordering Large Numbers
topics.concept:
To compare large numbers, first count the digits — more digits means a bigger number. If the digit-count is the same, compare from the left, place by place, until one digit is bigger.

Use >, < and =. To order numbers, compare in pairs, then line them up smallest-to-largest (ascending) or largest-to-smallest (descending).

examples.solution: Same up to thousands; hundreds 2 < 8, so 45,210 < 45,800.

recap: More digits means a bigger number.
Same digits → compare from the left, place by place.
Ascending = smallest first; descending = largest first.

topics.title: Rounding Numbers
topics.concept:
Rounding makes a number simpler but close to its value. Look at the digit just to the right of the place you are rounding to:

  • If it is 5 or more, round up.
  • If it is 4 or less, round down (keep it the same).

Example: 47 rounded to the nearest 10 → the ones digit 7 is 5+, so round up to 50.
topics.visual: <svg viewBox="0 0 420 110" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="width:100%;max-width:420px"><rect width="420" height="110" rx="14" fill="#ecfeff"/><line x1="30" y1="60" x2="390" y2="60" stroke="#0891b2" stroke-width="3"/><text stroke="none" x="30" y="85" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#0e7490">40</text><text stroke="none" x="390" y="85" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#0e7490">50</text><circle cx="282" cy="60" r="6" fill="#dc2626"/><text stroke="none" x="282" y="42" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#dc2626">47</text><text stroke="none" x="210" y="103" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#0e7490">47 is closer to 50</text></svg>

examples.solution: Ones digit 3 is 4 or less → round down to 60.
Tens digit 4 is 4 or less → round down to 300.

recap: Look at the digit to the right of the rounding place.
5 or more → round up; 4 or less → round down.
Rounding gives a number that is simpler but close.
